title: How Clarksburg New Construction Loads Drywall Dust Into Air Ducts
headline: Cabin Branch pads, Village HOAs, and why first-owner supplies still blow gypsum
description: Clarksburg, MD is Montgomery County’s I-270 north boom. Learn why new-construction ducts hold drywall dust, and when to clean them from Bethesda.

sections.heading: Clarksburg looks finished from the street. The ducts often are not.
paragraphs: Clarksburg Village, Cabin Branch, Town Center, Skylark, then lanes toward Damascus: a lot of the housing is first- or second-owner from the last two decades. Builders tape registers. Dust still gets in. Fine gypsum rides every return the first summers you live there. Damascus is a community we already drive, not its own page.
I-270 traffic grit does not wait for the last pad to finish. Filters catch some of it. Supplies still blow a gray film onto new paint. Humid seasons then glue that powder to cool trunks.

sections.heading: A new house is not a clean HVAC system
paragraphs: Builders run the air handler to dry mud and keep crews comfortable. That air is full of fines. They settle in the trunks. You move in, change a filter, and still get dusty registers. The dust was already downstream of the filter. HOA townhomes add long dryer vents and tight closets on top of that construction load.
If you moved in during a nearby build-out and the air still feels like a job site, start with [air duct cleaning in Clarksburg, MD](/locations/clarksburg).

sections.heading: Typical signs in a Clarksburg house
listItems: White or gray film on supplies in a house less than ten years old.
Dust returning onto new paint a week after you wipe the registers.
Long dry times in a Cabin Branch or Village townhome closet.

sections.heading: Farther up I-270 than Germantown — not a Town Center suite
paragraphs: Clarksburg is served from our [Bethesda](/locations/bethesda) office. Nearby [Germantown](/locations/germantown) and [Frederick](/locations/frederick) use the same Maryland crew. There is no Clarksburg storefront.

listItems: Ask for a duct cleaning after you close, not five years later.
Change filters more often while neighboring pads are still going up.
Clear HOA dryer vents about once a year.

faq.q: Why are new Clarksburg houses dusty inside the ducts?
faq.a: Construction fines are pulled into returns while nearby lots are still being finished. Filters do not catch all of it. The trunks store the rest until they are cleaned.
